extracted.intended_audience: computer vision and machine learning researchers and practitioners (especially vision transformer developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Research on improving Vision Transformer (ViT) position encoding to enable generalization and extrapolation to higher-resolution images, via directed attention using 2D attention masks. The paper proposes a method (LookHere) and reports quantitative evaluation on classification, adversarial robustness, calibration, and extrapolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation-equivariance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation-equivariance is presented as a desirable property of the position-encoding replacement; it is achieved by restricting attention heads to fixed fields of view pointed in different directions using 2D attention masks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention head diversity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method enforces diversity among attention heads by assigning different fixed fields of view and directions, which the authors argue helps limit distribution shift and improves extrapolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit distribution shift when extrapolating
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits the distribution shift that attention heads face when extrapolating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core design goal: by constraining attention heads' receptive fields via directed 2D masks, LookHere reduces the distributional mismatch encountered when test images contain more patches than training images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed attention via fixed 2D fields of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict attention heads to fixed fields of view, pointed in different directions, using 2D attention masks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central architectural change: a drop-in replacement for existing position encodings that uses 2D attention masks to direct each head's attention to a particular spatial neighborhood and orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drop-in replacement compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A drop-in replacement for the position encoding of plain ViTs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LookHere is positioned as compatible with plain ViT architectures without requiring wholesale architectural changes, enabling straightforward adoption (i.e., swap-in for existing position encoding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrapolation capability to larger images / more patches
rubrics_metrics.description: ViTs should extrapolate to more patches at test time; LookHere aims to improve this extrapolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper highlights that plain ViTs 'poorly extrapolate to more patches at test time' and evaluates extrapolation performance, notably when trained at 224^2 px and tested at 1024^2 px.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification performance (ImageNet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improves performance on classification (avg. 1.6% on ImageNet without extrapolation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as an empirical evaluation metric demonstrating LookHere's effectiveness on standard classification benchmarks; used to compare against baseline position encoding methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversarial robustness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adversarial robustness is measured and reported as an average improvement, indicating that the directed-attention approach can also help against adversarial perturbations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibration error reduction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration error is treated as a quality metric for model reliability; LookHere reports average reductions in calibration error compared to baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extrapolation performance vs 2D-RoPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Outperforms the current SoTA position encoding method, 2D-RoPE, by 21.7% on ImageNet when trained at 224^2 px and tested at 1024^2 px.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific cross-resolution extrapolation improvement is reported as strong evidence of LookHere's superiority for high-resolution generalization; it defines an evaluation scenario (train at 224^2, test at 1024^2) for measuring extrapolation ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of a high-resolution test set (ImageNet-HR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of a high-resolution test set to improve the evaluation of high-resolution image classifiers, called ImageNet-HR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a dedicated high-resolution benchmark is presented as important for properly evaluating extrapolation and generalization to larger images; the dataset itself is a contribution for empirical assessment.
